title: Nano Banana Pro Asset Pipeline
author: AvailableProcess2059
selftext:
I keep seeing people say use Nano Banana Pro for asset generation but most threads are thin on details. 

If you have a workflow that goes from idea to animated 2d or 3d assets please share in here so we can all benefit.

  
cheers!

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
Using a normal AI model like Nano Banana wont work for spritesheets and pixel art, because AI models cant output transparency, and image models alone have no understanding of animation.

Most pixel-sprite AIs (like Retro Diffusion) are pretty limited. They’re mainly tuned for bipedal humans and usually only give you idle/walk cycles, which breaks down fast once you need monsters, turrets, creatures, vehicles, or non-humanoid stuff.

That gap is actually why I built GameLab Studio (https://gamelabstudio.co). It’s designed for game assets, not just characters, and it’ll generate consistent pixel-art sprites, animations and full transparent bg spritesheets for anything: creatures, machines, towers, VFX, projectiles, etc. Animations aren’t locked to walk/idle either; you can generate attack, fire, spin, explode, transform, whatever the gameplay needs.

It also enforces consistency across scale, palette, and angles, by using already generated angles of the same asset for reference, so you don’t end up with “AI asset soup” during prototyping.

We also have a seamless tileable edge-aware texture generation model

replies.author: Defiant_Medicine_823
replies.body:
I uploaded an image, chose the direction I wanted to generate the animation in, it generates it in the same 3/4 view of the original image I uploaded and ignored the bottom view I requested. Then there is no clear way to preview or download the sprite sheet, or edit the frames. There is no coherent workflow for production. The animation result was clean and looked good otherwise, but that is standard with wan 2.2. 


My honest suggestion would be to treat this like a professional pipeline for heavy production or make it BYOK because I would not pay for something like this.

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body:
Thank you, I will try to rethink the way that ui is put together to make that more clear.

For now, I see where you were confused. Uploading an image like you did will use that image as the reference for the angle and subject orientation that is currently set. 

To accomplish what you were trying to do, you should have gone in to generate image, added your image as a reference, and then it would generate the reference image for the angle you selected. Then proceed to generate the animation.

To preview or download the spritesheets, there is a preview and download button below the generated spritesheet in the spritesheet box. Also an edit button in the same spot

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body:
Thank you, that’s a valid criticism. I think I can increase the free tokens a bit to account for the experimentation phase as you put it.

In terms of the ui ux, a user above has made a good point, and I will revise that bit of the ui to avoid confusion. Is there something specific you felt was confusing about the ui to you?

replies.author: vorty92
replies.body:
unless you intend to give a few hundred free generations, increasing the amount of free tokens "a bit" wouldn't solve it

token pricing feel quite unpredictable and is a huge turn off

also, I think your presentation could use some improvement... everything seems centered around one example which makes me, as a potential user, confused about what the tool is actually capable of

  
your example shows a big spritesheet (30+ frames) where the only difference frame to frame is minor details and some smoke

if your claim is that you're filling the retro diffusion gap, you should be showing attack/run/transform animations for monsters, robots, etc  
  
right now it feels like you're making claims that the user actually has to pay to even validate which definitely doesnt constitute a good UX

display a good amount of various examples, switch to a subscription based model, give a week of a free trial and I'd consider it

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body:
So, that is the create image dialog. 

First you create the base image for the camera view and subject orientation you selected.

Then you generate an animation that animates the base image.

Then you export that animation as a spritesheet. It is in that spritesheet dialog box that you will find the options to create say a 5x5 grid with 5 rows and 5 cols
